Demand to release funds for National Health Mission for West Bengal
records.SM_Text:
Shri Prakash Chik Baraik: Funds under the National Health Mission (NHM) have become a point of concern in West Bengal. The State Government has allocated a significant Rs 1,300 crore in the current fiscal year, while the Centres contribution remains at Rs 280 crore. The Union is reportedly yet to release around Rs 826.72 crore earmarked for constructing Suswasthya Kendras (health and wellness centres) across Bengal.

The Union Government cited non-compliance with specific color-branding guidelines for Health and Wellness Centres. In West Bengal, government hospitals provide free tests, treatments, and medications, and the Swasthya Sathi health insurance scheme covers 2.5 crore families, benefiting 45 lakh individuals. The number of medical colleges has significantly increased from 10 in 2011 to 33.

With around 11,000 centres benefiting three lakh people daily in Bengal, it is crucial for the Central Government to reassess its position, eliminate color-branding requirements, and promptly release essential funds for the National Health Mission.

(Ends)
